title: Low-error two-source extraction at polylogarithmic min-entropy
summary: Construct an explicit low-error extractor for two independent sources that each have only polylogarithmic min-entropy.

formal_statement.body: Construct an explicit family $\operatorname{Ext}_n:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^{m(n)}$ such that, for every pair of independent $(n,k)$-sources $X,Y$ with $k=\operatorname{polylog}(n)$, the distribution $\operatorname{Ext}_n(X,Y)$ is within the source's low-error regime of $U_{m(n)}$. The construction must achieve the low-error guarantee in the standard model, not only polynomially small error or a model with a common reference string.

scope.domain: Explicit two-source randomness extractors for independent weak sources
assumptions: Explicitness and low error use the source conventions
No common reference string or computational assumption is available
scope.unresolved_remainder: Published later work gives a randomized construction in the common-reference-string model and requires linear min-entropy (with an additional $O(n/\log n)$ randomized guarantee). It does not provide the requested standard-model explicit construction for two polylogarithmic-min-entropy sources.

provenance.note: The TIT paper calls the low-error/polylogarithmic-min-entropy target long-standing but does not identify one primary paper containing the complete formulation.

progress.summary: The TIT source states that an explicit low-error two-source extractor for polylogarithmic min-entropy remains a long-standing open question.

Later work constructs an efficient randomized strong two-source non-malleable extractor in a common-reference-string model, but its extra setup and higher entropy requirement leave the standard-model polylogarithmic target open.
